instruction: The parser maintainer needs a triage-ready summary before the next test rerun. Use `/tmp/code/test_output.txt` on the first Linux machine and `/tmp/code/maintainer.csv` on the second to create an unsent plain-text RFC 5322 email draft at `/tmp/code/test_failure_summary.eml` on the second machine. Address only the responsible maintainer, with no Cc or Bcc recipients, use a clear failure-summary subject, and summarize only the failed tests, including the module and test name; do not send it.

result.command:
python3 - <<'PY'
from email import policy
from email.parser import BytesParser
from email.utils import getaddresses
import re
try:
    with open('/tmp/code/test_failure_summary.eml', 'rb') as handle:
        message = BytesParser(policy=policy.default).parse(handle)
    to = [address.casefold() for _, address in getaddresses(message.get_all('to', []))]
    cc = [address.casefold() for _, address in getaddresses(message.get_all('cc', []))]
    bcc = [address.casefold() for _, address in getaddresses(message.get_all('bcc', []))]
    subject = str(message.get('subject', '')).strip().casefold()
    subject_ok = re.search(r'\b(?:parser|test)\b', subject) and re.search(r'\bfail(?:ed|ing|ure|ures)?\b', subject)
    if message.is_multipart():
        plain_parts = [part for part in message.walk() if part.get_content_type() == 'text/plain' and part.get_content_disposition() != 'attachment']
        other_text = [part for part in message.walk() if part.get_content_maintype() == 'text' and part.get_content_type() != 'text/plain' and part.get_content_disposition() != 'attachment']
        body = '\n'.join(str(part.get_content()) for part in plain_parts)
        plain_ok = len(plain_parts) == 1 and not other_text
    else:
        body = str(message.get_content())
        plain_ok = message.get_content_type() == 'text/plain'
    lowered = body.casefold()
    mentioned = set(re.findall(r'\btest_[a-z0-9_]+\b', lowered))
    clauses = [item.strip() for item in re.split(r'[\n\r]+|(?<=[.!?])\s+', lowered) if item.strip()]
    test_clauses = [item for item in clauses if re.search(r'\btest_parse_dates\b', item)]
    failed = any(re.search(r'\b(?:fail(?:ed|ing|ure)?|error)\b', item) for item in test_clauses)
    contradictory = any(re.search(r'\b(?:passed|passing|successful|not failing|did not fail|no failure|maybe|perhaps|possibly|might|pending|uncertain|unknown)\b', item) or '?' in item for item in test_clauses)
    ok = to == ['maintainer@example.test'] and not cc and not bcc and bool(subject_ok) and plain_ok
    ok = ok and mentioned == {'test_parse_dates'} and 'parser.py' in lowered and failed and not contradictory
except Exception:
    ok = False
print('present' if ok else 'missing')
PY

candidate_triage.rationale: An unsent RFC 5322 draft is a durable handoff artifact; scoring parses the sole recipient and failure-oriented subject, then classifies each mentioned test line so the failed set is exactly parser.py::test_parse_dates and test_basic_ok is allowed only as explicitly passed.

metadata.lite_evaluator_hardening_note: Body parsing binds parser.py and test_parse_dates on one line, requires explicit failed/failure/error polarity, rejects passed or negated-failure wording for that test, rejects unknown tests, and permits test_basic_ok only with an unambiguous passed status.
